result.note: Tests who became chief minister after the May 2026 assembly elections and structural firsts (TVK's debut, Sarma's second term, Rangaswamy's fifth term). Portfolio lists are skipped as too granular.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs of states or Union Territories and the chief ministers who took office after the assembly elections of May 2026:
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three are correctly matched. Adhikari, a former TMC leader who defected to the BJP in 2020, replaced Mamata Banerjee. Satheesan, a five-term MLA and former Leader of Opposition, became Kerala's chief minister, and Rangaswamy returned in Puducherry.
questions.source: Kerala’s new Chief Minister is V.D. Satheesan, a five-term member of the legislative assembly and former Leader of Opposition.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the outcome of the state assembly elections declared in May 2026:
items: In Tamil Nadu, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) emerged as the single largest party in its debut election.
In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma began his second consecutive term as Chief Minister.
In Puducherry, N. Rangaswamy began his fourth term as Chief Minister.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because Rangaswamy began his fifth term as Puducherry's chief minister, not his fourth. TVK, led by actor C. Joseph Vijay, did not exist two years earlier yet became the single largest party, while Sarma, who joined the BJP from Congress in 2015, returned for a second consecutive term.
questions.source: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), a party that did not exist two years ago, into the single largest party in its debut election.
